nodes.label: v0.2 re-scoped to an evidence phase; CI (#42), graph consistency and kg status (#37), mandatory descriptions (#36), kg query/impact (#38) and the benchmark harness (#39)
nodes.description:
Goal: turn external feedback into a short v0.2 'evidence phase' and deliver its reliability and query prerequisites before the benchmark.
Instructions: user writes in Spanish, everything versioned in English; commit per issue on its own branch, push/PR only when the user says so; stop before anything that costs money (LLM calls); do not touch the chore/33-cleanup branch.
Discoveries: RF-77 git-commit staleness fails when graph.json is committed (content digests instead); kg edit --id cannot fix kept nodes; WORKFLOWS_TOKEN first lacked Contents write; extraction time is linear (~0.7 ms/function); kg impact without --depth is very broad (120 elements for kg.store.load_graph); no Anthropic credentials on the machine.
Accomplished: issues #41 (site proposal), #42, #43 opened; #37/#38/#39 extended; PRs #44 (requirements 1.2 + roadmap), #45 (CI), #46 (#37 + kg status), #47 (#36), #48 (#38) merged; three demo queries posted on #40; bench/ harness with 6 pilot questions committed on feat/39-benchmark (ac0e96b), pushed, no PR.
Next steps: user installs .[bench] and provides ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then run the pilot, report and open the #39 PR; client approval of requirements 1.2 then v0.3 milestone/label and move #35/#18; demo #40; decide #41; regenerate docs/examples HTML.
Relevant files: docs/requirements.md, docs/roadmap.md, docs/query.md, docs/store.md, src/kg/update.py, src/kg/cli.py, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/smoke-test.sh, bench/

nodes.label: v0.2 is a time-boxed evidence phase (requirements 1.2 draft); order #43 -> #42/#37/#36 -> #38 -> #39 pilot -> #40, then #41
nodes.description:
What: requirements 1.2 (draft, pending client approval) cut v0.2 to RF-40-43, RF-72 (rebuild of parser layer is enough), RF-77 stale graph, RNF-03 user install, RNF-07 CI, RNF-10 benchmark outside the package; RF-13, RF-23, RF-31-33, RF-60-61, RF-73-74 and the Dockerfile move to v0.3; RF-44 topic views and RF-78 incremental extraction planned for v0.3; new section 8.2 success criteria, PA-05 and a change log; #35 and #18 move to v0.3.
Why: external feedback: go from 'an MVP that works on three repos' to evidence that kg solves a problem; old v0.2 was too broad and lacked stale graphs, coverage limits, CI and the benchmark.
Where: docs/requirements.md, docs/roadmap.md (issue order, Mermaid dependency diagram, benchmark design, exit questions, tentative v0.3 ordered by benchmark outcomes).
Learned: ~2-week time box, cut scope rather than extend; a negative benchmark result is valid; RF-13 (calls) comes back to v0.2 if impact with imports alone falls short; if the graph adds no value v0.3 starts with a redesign.

nodes.label: Issue #43: re-scope v0.2 requirements and plan v0.3 (merged via PR #44)
nodes.description:

Learned: docs/mvp-validation.md still says 'Open, for v0.2' on purpose: it is a historical record.

nodes.description:

Why: requirements v1.0 were client-approved, so changes are a pending version 1.2; CONTRIBUTING already names the label and milestone that do not exist yet.

Learned: PR #44 was merged while 1.2 still reads as pending approval.

nodes.label: Issue #42: CI, user install and edge-case tests (merged via PR #45)
nodes.description:
What: GitHub Actions workflow, clean-install smoke test, README user install and CI badge, 9 new edge-case tests (no store, empty graph.json, invalid UTF-8, coding: latin-1, broken/looping symlinks).
Why: tests only ran locally and the user install was undocumented and untested; protect behaviour before #38/#39.
Where: .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/smoke-test.sh, README.md, tests/
Learned: error handling was already good (no tracebacks, corrupt stores give actionable errors), so this was about automating and covering it; first CI run was green.

nodes.label: CI runs ruff + pytest on Python 3.12 and 3.13, plus a non-editable clean install with a smoke test
nodes.description:
What: on every push to main and every PR: ruff check, ruff format --check, pytest on 3.12 and 3.13; a separate job does pip install . (no dev extras) in a fresh venv and runs .github/smoke-test.sh (init, extract, add, validate, render HTML/PNG/SVG, status, query, impact, --json contract, bundled vis-network assets).
Why: requires-python is >=3.12 so 3.13 is free coverage; the user install path must be tested, not only the dev one.
Where: .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/smoke-test.sh (also runnable locally)
Learned: every new CLI command should be added to the smoke test.

nodes.label: Pushing .github/workflows needs WORKFLOWS_TOKEN (Contents + Workflows write), used via a temporary askpass
nodes.description:
What: a separate fine-grained token WORKFLOWS_TOKEN in .env is used to push branches that touch .github/workflows/; it must have Contents and Workflows read/write on Cristian1A/kg.
Why: the regular GITHUB_TOKEN lacks the workflow scope; the first WORKFLOWS_TOKEN returned 403 even on --dry-run pushes because it lacked Contents write; the user fixed its permissions.
Where: .env (read variable names only, never values)
Learned: push through a temporary askpass script with credential cache off so the token never lands in the URL or git config; test permissions with git push --dry-run.

nodes.label: Extraction time on a 50,000-function file: 37 s, 515 MB, linear at ~0.7 ms per function
nodes.description:
What: edge-case probe during #42 with a very large generated Python file.
Why: check whether a huge file is a bug or just slow.
Where: kg extract (src/kg/extract/python.py)
Learned: growth is linear, not a bug; revisit only if RNF-06 targets require it.

nodes.label: Spanish leftovers in tests/test_store.py break rule 8
nodes.description:
What: the comment '# --- errores ---' and the string 'contenido previo' remain in tests/test_store.py.
Why: missed by the English migration and #33 cleanup.
Where: tests/test_store.py
Learned: one-line fix offered during #42; the user did not ask for it, so it is still open.

nodes.label: kg extract prunes kg's own parser elements it no longer produces, in one atomic write with the merge
nodes.description:
What: before merging, remove elements with method parser from extractors python-ast, pyproject and requirements that the new extraction does not produce; never remove llm/manual knowledge, parser elements of other tools, elements of files skipped this time (syntax error), or a derived node still used by an agent edge (kept and reported); if the store holds another repo's extraction nothing is removed and a warning is shown; kg extract --dry-run shows added/merged/removed; --json gains changed, dry_run, removed.
Why: kg add never removes, so deleted/renamed/moved code stayed in the store; full rebuild of the parser layer chosen over incremental update because extraction is ~1 s per 100 files and correctness comes first (incremental is RF-78, v0.3).
Where: src/kg/update.py, src/kg/cli.py, docs/store.md, docs/extract.md
Learned: a move or rename is a delete plus an add because IDs come from paths and qualified names; with pruning disabled 9 of 26 scenario tests fail; on a copy of samples/basic-python-cli it removed 4 stale nodes and 10 edges and kept the one node with agent edges.

nodes.label: Kept derived nodes with agent edges are fixed by re-adding the edges to the new ID with kg add, then kg remove of the old node
nodes.description:
What: the extract report, docs and agent guide tell the user to resend the agent edges pointing to the new ID with kg add and then kg remove the old node.
Why: the first documented fix, kg edit --id, fails because the new ID already exists after the extract.
Where: src/kg/update.py messages, docs/store.md, src/kg/agents/guide.md
Learned: the add-then-remove path was tested end to end.

nodes.label: Stale-graph detection (RF-77) uses per-file content digests and a new kg status, not the git commit
nodes.description:
What: File and Config nodes store attrs.digest (short SHA-256); kg status [path] lists files modified, added or deleted since the last extraction; kg query/impact reuse it as the stale_graph note.
Why: the drafted design recorded the git commit, but committing graph.json moves HEAD so a versioned graph would look stale forever; digests also work without git. kg validate has no --kg-dir, so the warning could not live there as #37/RF-77 first said.
Where: src/kg/update.py, src/kg/extract/files.py, docs/store.md, RF-77 in docs/requirements.md
Learned: an unparseable file keeps its previous digest so it stays 'modified' until fixed; a changed digest is not reported as a merge conflict.

nodes.label: Issue #37: keep the graph consistent when the code changes (merged via PR #46)
nodes.description:
What: derived-layer pruning on kg extract, --dry-run, kg status with content digests; 26 scenario tests in tests/test_update.py.
Why: stale parser nodes made queries and the benchmark unreliable.
Where: src/kg/update.py, tests/test_update.py
Learned: done 2026-10-13; see decision:extract-replaces-derived-layer and decision:stale-detection-by-content-digest.

nodes.label: Agent-created nodes must have a description: missing_description warning, guide section, HTML search over descriptions
nodes.description:
What: kg validate and kg add warn missing_description for llm nodes with no or empty description; the guide makes descriptions mandatory and explains describing undocumented extracted nodes (send the existing ID and type with llm provenance; parser provenance is kept, a later docstring wins); HTML search also matches descriptions, ranked after names and IDs.
Why: a node with only an ID and label sends the reader back to the source; descriptions make the graph searchable by meaning and matter for the benchmark.
Where: src/kg/schema/validation.py, src/kg/agents/guide.md, src/kg/render/assets/template.html, docs/schema.md, docs/render.md
Learned: a warning, not an error; the search is tested in headless Chrome and fails without the change; a test checks examples/agent/*.json have descriptions.

nodes.label: Issue #36: mandatory descriptions for agent-created nodes (merged via PR #47)
nodes.description:
What: missing_description warning, guide Descriptions section, HTML search over descriptions, two descriptions added to examples/basic-repo.json.
Why: needed before measuring in the benchmark.
Where: src/kg/schema/validation.py, src/kg/agents/guide.md
Learned: done 2026-10-13; touched the same guide lines as #37 but merged without conflicts (371 tests on the combined tree).

nodes.label: Regenerate the HTML pages in docs/examples so they search descriptions
nodes.description:
What: rerun kg render --html for the published examples.
Why: they were generated before #36 changed the template, so their search ignores descriptions.
Where: docs/examples/*.html (GitHub Pages)
Learned: left out of #36 on purpose because it was not in scope.

nodes.label: kg query (node/find/path/untested/undocumented) and kg impact walk relations backwards with containment and coverage-limit notes
nodes.description:
What: kg query node|find|path|untested|undocumented; path tries forward, backward, then mixed and says which; kg impact walks calls, depends_on, documents, implements, imports, justifies, tests backwards, plus containment (a changed function/class reaches its defining module/class; --no-containment), --relation replaces the list and custom relations propagate only when listed; each result has depth, direct flag, justifying path, provenance and weakest confidence; every answer carries notes stale_graph, freshness_unknown, unread_files, missing_relations; empty answers say 'no relation found in the graph'; unknown IDs exit 2 with the closest ID.
Why: RF-40-43 and the benchmark/demo need a query interface; impact must never present possible effects as certain.
Where: src/kg/analysis.py, src/kg/cli.py, docs/query.md (--json output documented as stable), guide section 'Answering questions with the graph'
Learned: find ranks like the HTML short() rule (unlabeled nodes tie and sort by ID); with containment disabled 4 tests fail; no external query engine.

nodes.label: Issue #38: kg query and kg impact (merged via PR #48)
nodes.description:
What: query and impact commands, docs/query.md, guide section, smoke test, 27 tests in tests/test_query.py.
Why: prerequisite of the benchmark (#39) and demo (#40).
Where: src/kg/analysis.py, src/kg/cli.py
Learned: done 2026-10-13; three example queries posted on #40.

nodes.label: kg impact with no --depth follows imports transitively and returns very broad results
nodes.description:
What: on kg itself a change to kg.store.load_graph reaches 120 elements; --depth 2 or 3 is usually more useful to agents.
Why: impact follows imports transitively by default; correct but noisy.
Where: src/kg/analysis.py (kg impact default depth)
Learned: whether to limit the default depth is to be decided from the benchmark (#39).

nodes.label: Issue #40: reproducible demo with queries on a real repo (prio:v0.2)
nodes.description:
What: demo flow on a docs/examples repo: clone, kg init/extract, kg add the committed examples/agent layer, render, three queries with reference answers; no LLM needed.
Why: a new user should see how kg answers questions without a long explanation.
Where: GitHub issue #40 comment; future demo doc
Learned: three queries already posted on #40 for my_first_data_project at 3d57177: kg query untested, kg impact function:etl.utils.get_postgres_connection --depth 2, kg query node module:etl.utils; comes after the benchmark in the roadmap.

nodes.label: Benchmark harness: same model/prompt/turn limit for code and graph agents, manual tool loop, mechanical grading, no fallback model
nodes.description:
What: bench/ runs each question twice: code strategy (list/read/search tools) and graph strategy (read-only kg tool over the store); manual tool-use loop records token usage per request, caps turns, ends with submit_answer; prepare clones the three example repos at pinned commits into bench/.cache and builds stores with kg extract plus examples/agent layers; grading is F1 over normalized names for list questions (etl/utils.py, module:etl.utils, etl.utils equal), keyword groups otherwise, traceability = share of cited evidence that exists; runs appended to JSONL with full config; bench.report shows quality and cost separately.
Why: RNF-10/RF-24 keep LLM calls out of kg; mechanical grading avoids an LLM judge; no fallback model so both strategies always use the same model (a refusal counts as failure).
Where: bench/agent.py, bench/tools.py, bench/grading.py, bench/run.py, bench/report.py, bench/questions/pilot.json, bench/repos.json; anthropic is an optional extra 'bench'
Learned: 6 pilot questions with references checked against the code, not the graph (the graph links two test files to sqlalchemy they do not import); tests use a fake client so CI needs no key; SDK 1.13 accepts all request parameters.

nodes.label: Benchmark also compares topic-specific graphs and old vs. recent commits, including a stale graph
nodes.description:
What: questions tagged by topic (documentation, tests, development, decisions); at least one topic graph or view compared with the full graph and the baseline; at least one repo measured on two commits, including an old graph queried about recent code.
Why: user request: a single generic graph could hide where the graph helps; across commits shows whether value holds as the repo grows and whether stale warnings prevent wrong claims.
Where: issue #39 'Additional variants to evaluate'; docs/roadmap.md benchmark design
Learned: views of one store filtered by node/edge type are preferred over separate graphs (no repeated extraction, kg render already filters); fewer questions per cell, so the report must state sample-size limits; topic views as a product feature are RF-44 in v0.3 only if the benchmark shows value.

nodes.label: Issue #39: reproducible benchmark, code vs. knowledge graph (prio:v0.2)
nodes.description:
What: harness and 6 pilot questions committed on feat/39-benchmark (ac0e96b, stacked on #38, pushed, no PR, commit uses Refs: #39); next run the pilot (6 questions x 2 strategies, claude-opus-5-5, medium effort), then grow to 15-30 questions with topic and commit variants and write the report.
Why: the most valuable v0.2 item: evidence of whether kg helps an agent; a negative result is valid.
Where: bench/, bench/README.md
Learned: running needs pip install -e .[bench] (not done in env/) and Anthropic credentials, which do not exist on the machine; the run costs money so it waits for the user's go-ahead; PR opens with the results.

nodes.label: Benchmark runs call a paid LLM: wait for the user's go-ahead and credentials
nodes.description:
What: do not run anything that calls an LLM without the user's explicit OK; no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, .env entry or ant CLI exists on the machine.
Why: LLM calls cost money; the user said to do only what can be done without him.
Where: bench/run.py, .env
Learned: estimated a few dollars for the 12-run pilot, unmeasured.

nodes.label: Issue #41 (proposal, not validated): project-wide Pages landing page or a Streamlit app for results
nodes.description:
What: option A a static landing page at cristian1a.github.io/kg/ linking docs and examples; option B a Streamlit app (e.g. Community Cloud) presenting example graphs and later demo/benchmark results; both compatible.
Why: Pages only serves example graphs and the root URL shows nothing.
Where: docs/ (Pages from main:/docs), README, repo About
Learned: labeled type:docs, prio:futuro, no milestone; a hosted app conflicts with requirements section 9 ('a web server or graph hosting' out of scope) and would need an explicit exception; decide after the demo (#40); existing example URLs must keep working.

nodes.label: Decide how to clean the samples/basic-python-cli store with stale parser-provenance nodes
nodes.description:
What: store has stale parser-provenance nodes and old-model edges from hand-written JSON; options were recreate or keep.
Why: kg add never deleted, so stale elements stayed.
Where: samples/basic-python-cli/.kg (ignored by git)
Learned: since #37 a plain kg extract cleans it: on a copy it removed 4 stale nodes and 10 edges and kept the one node used by agent edges; the real store has still not been touched, pending the user.
